messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: plotNuse (Quality Assessment Model)
parts:
Hi, I think Ken said that the Quality Assessment Model is going to be
removed because Henrik had code that did the Nuse plots already? Is that
available?

Also, I don't remember if this is what the last message is about -- I
couldn't find it again -- but looking at the code for
plotNuse.QualityAssessmentModel(), it seems like you will not correctly
plot the outliers. Namely the code does (more or less)
for( each array kk ){
data <- ...
boxplotStats[[kk]] <- boxplot.stats(data)
}
bxpStats <- list()
elementNames <- names(boxplotStats[[1]])
for (name in elementNames) {
bxpStats[[name]] <- do.call("cbind", lapply(boxplotStats,
function(x) {x[[name]]})))
}
bxp(bxpStats, main = main, ...)

The idea is that the second for loop collapses the elements from each of
the individual boxplot calls (in the 1st for loop) into the form needed
for the command bxp. But my understand of bxp is that while the first
few elements are matrices with each column corresponding to a group (the
information for plotting the 'box' part of the boxplot), the elements
$out and $group expected by bxp are both vectors of length=(TOTAL
outliers in all groups) -- $out gives the value of the outlier and
$group gives which group the outlier is in. (groups are the different
boxplots). So there will not be the correct form -- and a matrix
wouldn't work anyway since the number of outliers from each group would
be different.

I understand from the previous email that this set of functions isn't
really being supported anymore, but could someone at least confirm that
my analysis is correct or not, because I know some people are using
these functions for the plots.

Thanks,
Elizabeth

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] plotNuse (Quality Assessment Model)
parts:
> Hi, I think Ken said that the Quality Assessment Model is going to be
> removed because Henrik had code that did the Nuse plots already? Is that
> available?

That's not quite right. _Some_ of the stuff in QualityAssessmentModel is
implemented elsewhere and will be removed (e.g. calculation of weights).
plotNuse() and plotRle() will be retained, but maybe not as methods belonging
to QualityAssessmentModel. This hasn't been decided yet.

> Also, I don't remember if this is what the last message is about -- I
> couldn't find it again -- but looking at the code for
> plotNuse.QualityAssessmentModel(), it seems like you will not correctly
> plot the outliers.

You're right, and thanks for noticing this. I have fixed the bug so that
outliers are now correctly treated. I've also made both plotNuse() and
plotRle() return (invisibly) the boxplot statistics.

Cheers,

Ken
